why: One step quietly exempted from the player's UI scale. This is the shape a tidy-up takes -- `0.8125rem` is the value the step has always had and reads as a simplification of a noisy `calc()`, while every other step keeps its multiplier so the feature still visibly works. A reviewer comparing a 150% capture against a 100% one would see the interface grow and not notice that one size did not. It is pinned because the guard has to count the steps rather than spot-check one: a step that loses its multiplier simply stops matching the scaled pattern, so an assertion written only over the matches would pass on the survivors.
killedBy: hud.css type scales with the reader (issue #971) spends every step of the scale, and each step is a whole number of px at the default
